headline: There is no single American drug supply. There are at least four.
summary: Of 90 substances detected routinely in mail-in drug checking, only 20 turn up everywhere at similar rates. The other 70 are concentrated — some 80 to 90 percent confined to a single region. A substance is counted as regional when one region holds at least 35% of its national signal.
caveat: This is not a random sample of the US drug supply. It is what reaches harm reduction programs and drug-checking partners, and that coverage is uneven — strong in some states, thin in others.

source.name: UNC Street Drug Analysis Lab
source.attribution: UNC Street Drug Analysis Lab at opioiddata.org

substances.name: phenethyl chloride
substances.desc: A fentanyl synthesis precursor that signals clandestine manufacturing activity.

substances.name: diphenhydramine
substances.desc: Benadryl, a sedating antihistamine added to opioids to enhance sedation and to compensate for shorter-acting opioids.

substances.name: noramidopyrine
substances.desc: An industrial precursor compound related to certain fentanyl synthesis routes.

substances.name: aniline
substances.desc: A basic industrial chemical used as a starting material in fentanyl precursor synthesis.

substances.name: norcocaine
substances.desc: A metabolite and synthesis byproduct of cocaine that signals less-refined product or aggressive cutting practices.

substances.name: phenacetin
substances.desc: A discontinued analgesic widely used as a cocaine cutting agent because its appearance and properties mimic powder cocaine.

substances.name: procaine
substances.desc: A local anesthetic added to cocaine to mimic the numbing effect of pure cocaine when tasted.

substances.name: diacetamate
substances.desc: A synthesis-related compound that appears as a manufacturing impurity.

substances.name: N-butyl-aniline
substances.desc: A synthesis byproduct that appears in less-refined cocaine.

substances.name: non-specific sugar
substances.desc: Generic sugars (lactose, sucrose, glucose) used as inexpensive cuts in powder drug supplies.

substances.name: tropacocaine
substances.desc: A natural alkaloid from the coca plant that appears in less-refined cocaine product.

substances.name: N,N-dimethylpentylone
substances.desc: A synthetic cathinone ('bath salt') with stimulant effects, recently emerging as an adulterant in MDMA and other supplies.

substances.name: 1,3-Diacetin
substances.desc: A glycerin derivative used industrially as a humectant and solvent; appears in some drug supplies as a cut or carrier.

substances.name: protonitazene
substances.desc: A novel nitazene-family synthetic opioid that has appeared in the supply as an emerging fentanyl alternative.

substances.name: p-fluoro phenethyl 4-ANPP
substances.desc: A precursor specific to p-fluorofentanyl manufacture, indicating that synthesis route.

substances.name: tetracaine
substances.desc: A potent local anesthetic used as a cocaine bulking agent, producing the numbing sensation associated with cocaine quality.

substances.name: medetomidine
substances.desc: Another veterinary alpha-2 sedative now appearing in the fentanyl supply, with effects similar to xylazine and not reversed by naloxone.

substances.name: 2C-B
substances.desc: A phenethylamine psychedelic with stimulant and visual properties, popular in some recreational scenes.

substances.name: methyl ecgonidine (MED)
substances.desc: A cocaine pyrolysis product that forms when cocaine is smoked, also a marker of less-refined product.

substances.name: NPP
substances.desc: N-phenethyl-4-piperidone, the most common direct precursor used in clandestine fentanyl manufacture.

substances.name: quinine
substances.desc: A bitter alkaloid traditionally used as a heroin cutting agent to mimic heroin's bitter taste.

substances.name: benzyl benzoate
substances.desc: A solvent and plasticizer that can appear as a carrier or contaminant.

substances.name: niacinamide
substances.desc: Vitamin B3, used as a cheap inert bulking agent in powder drug supplies.

substances.name: dimethyl sulfone (methylsulfonylmethane MSM)
substances.desc: An over-the-counter supplement sold as a joint-health product, used as a methamphetamine cutting agent.

substances.name: benzoylecgonine (BZ)
substances.desc: The main human metabolite of cocaine, sometimes detected in samples as a marker of product handling or contamination.

substances.name: nicotine
substances.desc: Trace nicotine contamination can come from handling or paraphernalia; rarely a deliberate additive.

substances.name: clonazepam
substances.desc: Klonopin, a long-acting prescription benzodiazepine; combination with opioids substantially increases overdose risk.

substances.name: 1-[(2-chlorophenyl)(methylimino)methyl]cyclopentanol
substances.desc: A novel synthetic compound detected in recent supply samples whose pharmacology is poorly characterized.

substances.name: 2-Fluoro-2-oxo PCE
substances.desc: A novel dissociative compound in the PCP/ketamine family detected as an emerging substance.

substances.name: ortho-methylfentanyl
substances.desc: A fentanyl analog with high potency; its detection signals diversified or older-route synthesis.

substances.name: meconin
substances.desc: A minor alkaloid of opium present as a heroin manufacturing residue.

substances.name: erythritol
substances.desc: A sugar alcohol sweetener used as a bulking agent, especially in fentanyl supplies.

substances.name: phenethylbromide
substances.desc: An alkylating reagent used in fentanyl-class synthesis.

substances.name: benzyl alcohol
substances.desc: A preservative solvent occasionally used as a carrier in injection drug preparations.

substances.name: 1-phenethyl-4-hydroxypiperidine
substances.desc: A fentanyl precursor / synthesis intermediate detected as a manufacturing byproduct.

substances.name: acetanilide
substances.desc: A precursor and synthesis impurity, originally a historical fever medication.

substances.name: caffeine
substances.desc: A stimulant used as a bulking agent in MDMA, cocaine, and other stimulants to mimic perceived strength.

substances.name: benzocaine
substances.desc: A local anesthetic commonly added to cocaine and to powders sold as cocaine to fake the numbing test.

substances.name: dextromethorphan
substances.desc: An over-the-counter cough suppressant with dissociative effects at high doses; sometimes added to drug supplies.

substances.name: carfentanil
substances.desc: An extremely potent fentanyl analog (roughly 100 times stronger than fentanyl itself) originally developed as an elephant tranquilizer.

substances.name: tetramethyl-4-AP
substances.desc: A piperidine derivative whose pharmacology in the supply context is not well characterized.

substances.name: N,N-Dimethylamphetamine (DMA)
substances.desc: An amphetamine-class compound that appears as a methamphetamine impurity or as a distinct emerging substance.

substances.name: 1-propionyl-4-anilinopiperidine
substances.desc: A fentanyl-class synthesis intermediate that appears as a manufacturing impurity.

substances.name: despropionyl ortho-methylfentanyl
substances.desc: A synthesis precursor specific to ortho-methylfentanyl manufacture.

substances.name: N-propionyl norfentanyl
substances.desc: A fentanyl-related synthesis intermediate.

substances.name: levamisole
substances.desc: A veterinary deworming agent added to most cocaine in North America; chronic exposure can cause serious immune system damage and skin necrosis.

substances.name: tetramethylnorfentanyl
substances.desc: A novel fentanyl-related compound whose pharmacology is poorly characterized.

substances.name: oxycodone
substances.desc: A prescription opioid (OxyContin, Percocet) sometimes diverted into the unregulated supply.

substances.name: noscapine
substances.desc: A non-narcotic opium alkaloid that appears in heroin as a residue from opium poppy processing.

substances.name: xylazine
substances.desc: A veterinary sedative ('tranq') increasingly mixed into fentanyl; not reversed by naloxone, prolongs sedation, and causes severe skin wounds with chronic use.

substances.name: 4-anilinopiperidine
substances.desc: A core fentanyl precursor whose international trafficking has been increasingly restricted.

substances.name: melatonin
substances.desc: A sleep-cycle hormone available over the counter; rarely a deliberate drug additive, more often packaging or co-use signal.

substances.name: N,N-dimethyltryptamine (DMT)
substances.desc: A short-acting serotonergic psychedelic, smoked or vaporized; also the active ingredient of ayahuasca.

substances.name: phenazolam
substances.desc: A novel designer benzodiazepine related to bromazolam.

substances.name: MDA
substances.desc: A close relative of MDMA with similar effects; often appears alongside MDMA or as a substitute.

substances.name: N-phenylpropanamide
substances.desc: A fentanyl synthesis precursor whose presence flags clandestine fentanyl manufacture.

substances.name: 2,2,6,6-tetramethyl-4-piperidinol
substances.desc: A piperidine derivative used as a stabilizer in plastics manufacturing, occasionally appearing as a contaminant.

substances.name: papaverine
substances.desc: An opium-poppy alkaloid that appears as a heroin manufacturing residue, also used medically as a smooth muscle relaxant.

substances.name: acetaminophen
substances.desc: Tylenol, often co-formulated in prescription opioid pills and pressed into counterfeit pills as filler.

substances.name: acetyl fentanyl
substances.desc: An early fentanyl analog still detected in the supply, with potency comparable to fentanyl itself.

substances.name: phenethyl 4-ANPP
substances.desc: A fentanyl precursor that appears as a synthesis impurity in finished fentanyl product.

substances.name: 3,4-MDMA
substances.desc: MDMA / Molly / ecstasy, an empathogenic stimulant; supply purity and adulteration vary widely.

substances.name: heroin
substances.desc: A semi-synthetic opioid derived from morphine; now largely displaced by fentanyl in most U.S. markets but still present in some regions.

substances.name: metonitazene
substances.desc: A novel synthetic opioid from the nitazene family with potency comparable to fentanyl.

substances.name: bis(2,2,6,6-tetramethyl-4-piperidyl) sebacate
substances.desc: A hindered-amine plastic stabilizer (HALS) used in polymers; its presence is most likely a packaging contaminant.

substances.name: cocaine
substances.desc: A short-acting stimulant from coca leaves; quality and adulteration vary substantially by region and price point.

substances.name: bromazolam
substances.desc: A novel 'designer' benzodiazepine not approved for medical use, appearing in counterfeit pills and as an adulterant in opioids.

substances.name: 4-Anilino-1-Boc-piperidine
substances.desc: A protected form of the fentanyl precursor 4-anilinopiperidine, used to evade precursor controls.

substances.name: N-phenethyl-N-phenylpropionamide
substances.desc: A fentanyl precursor that appears as a manufacturing impurity.

substances.name: gabapentin
substances.desc: A non-opioid anticonvulsant increasingly co-detected with opioids; can potentiate sedation.

substances.name: ketamine
substances.desc: A dissociative anesthetic used both medically and recreationally; detected as a primary substance and occasionally as an adulterant.

substances.name: tramadol
substances.desc: A weaker prescription opioid that also acts on serotonin; detected in some unregulated supplies, especially internationally.

substances.name: ethyl 4-ANPP
substances.desc: A synthesis byproduct related to fentanyl manufacture using ethyl-substituted precursors.

substances.name: amphetamine
substances.desc: A pharmaceutical and recreational stimulant; can appear from prescription diversion or as a methamphetamine impurity.

substances.name: methamphetamine
substances.desc: A potent synthetic stimulant that has become widely co-present with fentanyl in many supplies, raising overdose and cardiovascular risk.

substances.name: lysergic acid diethylamide (LSD)
substances.desc: A classic serotonergic psychedelic, typically sold on blotter paper.

substances.name: 1-phenethyl-4-propionyloxypiperidine
substances.desc: A fentanyl synthesis intermediate that appears as a manufacturing impurity.

substances.name: alprazolam
substances.desc: Xanax, a prescription benzodiazepine increasingly diverted into the unregulated supply, often pressed into counterfeit pills.

substances.name: morphine
substances.desc: The principal alkaloid of opium and the parent compound of heroin; detection may reflect heroin, pharmaceutical diversion, or precursor presence.

substances.name: 6-monoacetylmorphine (6-MAM)
substances.desc: A specific metabolite and impurity of heroin; its presence confirms recent heroin (rather than morphine) in a sample.

substances.name: p-fluorofentanyl
substances.desc: A fentanyl analog with similar potency, increasingly common in the supply since the early 2020s.

substances.name: delta-9-THC
substances.desc: The primary psychoactive compound in cannabis.

substances.name: despropionyl p-fluorofentanyl
substances.desc: A precursor and degradation product specific to p-fluorofentanyl synthesis.

substances.name: glycerin
substances.desc: A neutral viscous liquid used as a carrier or to alter texture in pressed pills and oils.

substances.name: lidocaine
substances.desc: A widely used local anesthetic added to cocaine as a cut, also detected as a general adulterant across fentanyl and stimulant samples.

substances.name: cannabinol
substances.desc: A mildly sedating minor cannabinoid that forms when THC oxidizes; often detected in older cannabis material.

substances.name: mannitol
substances.desc: A sugar alcohol used as a bulking agent across cocaine, methamphetamine, and other powder supplies.

substances.name: 4-ANPP
substances.desc: The primary synthesis precursor and degradation product of fentanyl; its presence indicates fentanyl manufacturing.

substances.name: fentanyl
substances.desc: A synthetic opioid roughly 50 times more potent than heroin that now dominates the North American illicit opioid supply.

substances.name: acetylcodeine
substances.desc: A synthesis byproduct of heroin manufacture from opium, indicating heroin rather than synthetic opioid origin.
